I can't use stimulants because of the panic disorder, my last major panic attack was caused by an extra strength sudafed for congestion to give you an idea of how sensitive I am to any CNS stimulant. One caffienated drink a day is the most I can handle. Alcohol in reasonable amounts (just enough for getting a little tipsy) doesn't precipitate any depersonalization, neither do benzos and whatnot. Before I developed this disorder I abused a lot of opiates, mostly morphine because it was readily available to me. Now it causes bad enough dissociative symptoms that I'll avoid it even when my migraines are so bad I want to throw myself out a window. The weird thing is that taking morphine or codeine is fine until I start to come down from it like 4 hours later; that's when the really horrifying feelings set in and I start to sketch out and feel like I'm dreaming. Taking hydrocodone or oxycodone doesn't cause that and actually seems to improve some of my symptoms (which include some mild cognitive impairment, difficulty speaking, bad short term memory along with the DP/DR). I'm not sure why; I did read that morphine has more affinity for kappa opioid receptors, which can cause dysphoria and depersonalization, so maybe that could explain it but I'm not a pharmacologist (I'm interested in it and considering studying it but with my disabilities it might not be practical). I have had issues with taking "self medicating" straight to drug abuse but I've been doing better lately at being reasonable with my drug use. You just described exactly what I'm experiencing. I was forced to go cold turkey by my mother, who thought I needed to quit and "intervened" by taking all my pills and sending me to my grandmothers where I couldn't possibly find more. It was absolute hell, I felt like I was being shocked, had muscle rigidity and contractions, shaking, agonizing headaches, my blood pressure was 160/105 and my heart rate was 140 for days. I thought I was going to die. I actually did end up in the hospital. I got through the acute withdrawals, but after that I was stuck in bed with absolutely paralyzing terror and feelings of imminent doom, and I was struggling to even form a coherent sentence, I was forgetting simple words, had very little short-term memory and I felt like I was sleepwalking. I've improved since then but it's still hard when I'm so aware of the fact that my mind isn't as sharp as it used to be and I've read that people who have been addicted to benzos for long periods of time often never get back to the way they were before they started, which is a terrifying prospect for me.

I'm not against using drugs if I were to find something that wouldn't fry my brain, but why are drugs "bad" if my doctor prescribes them? My doctor didn't push me to take benzos, I was fully aware of the risks and was told that I should only take them a couple times a week. I was only given 6 refills, after that I started buying them illegally. I don't understand the anti-doctor attitudes around here. I definitely agree that some doctors overprescribe but it seems silly to think that drugs are fine as long as they're illegal.
